question.:question/problem:
Consider the following system of linear equations:

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x + 2 y + 5 z &=11 \\ 3 x + 8 y + 17 z &=41 \\ 2 x + 4 y + 10 z &=22\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Use the standard Gauss-Jordan method to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to reduced row echelon form.
question.:question/worked-solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 2 & 5 & 11 \\ 3 & 8 & 17 & 41 \\ 2 & 4 & 10 & 22\end{array}\right]
$$

First reduce the matrix to row echelon form, making each pivot equal to $1$.

$$
R_{2}:=R_{2}+\left(-3\right)R_{1}\qquad M\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 2 & 5 & 11 \\ 0 & 2 & 2 & 8 \\ 2 & 4 & 10 & 22\end{array}\right]
$$



$$
R_{3}:=R_{3}+\left(-2\right)R_{1}\qquad M\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 2 & 5 & 11 \\ 0 & 2 & 2 & 8 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{array}\right]
$$



$$
R_{2}:=\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)R_{2}\qquad M\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 2 & 5 & 11 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & 4 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{array}\right]
$$

In the row echelon form above, we have only two pivots (in the $1$st and $2$nd columns). To transform the matrix to reduced row echelon form, we need to create zeros above the pivots only.

$$
R_{1}:=R_{1}+\left(-2\right)R_{2}\qquad M\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 0 & 3 & 3 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & 4 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{array}\right]
$$

question.:question/problem:
Consider the following system of linear equations:

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x - 2 y - 3 z &=-8 \\ 2 x - 5 y - 7 z &=-19 \\ - x + 2 y + 3 z &=8\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Use the standard Gauss-Jordan method to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to reduced row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.
question.:question/worked-solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -2 & -3 & -8 \\ 2 & -5 & -7 & -19 \\ -1 & 2 & 3 & 8\end{array}\right]
$$

First reduce the matrix to row echelon form, making each pivot equal to $1$.

$$
R_{2}:=R_{2}+\left(-2\right)R_{1}\qquad M\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -2 & -3 & -8 \\ 0 & -1 & -1 & -3 \\ -1 & 2 & 3 & 8\end{array}\right]
$$



$$
R_{3}:=R_{3}+\left(1\right)R_{1}\qquad M\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -2 & -3 & -8 \\ 0 & -1 & -1 & -3 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{array}\right]
$$



$$
R_{2}:=\left(-1\right)R_{2}\qquad M\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -2 & -3 & -8 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{array}\right]
$$

In the row echelon form above, we have only two pivots (in the $1$st and $2$nd columns). To transform the matrix to reduced row echelon form, we need to create zeros above the pivots only.

$$
R_{1}:=R_{1}+\left(2\right)R_{2}\qquad M\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 0 & -1 & -2 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{array}\right]
$$

The corresponding system is now

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x - z &=-2 \\ y + z &=3 \\ 0 &=0\end{aligned}\right.
$$

The final equation is $0=0$, so it imposes no restriction. The basic variables are $x$ and $y$, and the free variable is $z$. Find $x$ and $y$ in terms of $z$. Therefore, the general solution is

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x &=z - 2 \\ y &=3 - z \\ z &=z\end{aligned}\right.
$$

where $z$ is an arbitrary real number. In vector form, the solution can be written as

$$
\begin{bmatrix}x \\ y \\ z\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}z - 2 \\ 3 - z \\ z\end{bmatrix},\,z\in (-\infty ,\infty )
$$

$$
M=\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}4 & -11 & -23 & -33 \\ 1 & -3 & -6 & -9 \\ -3 & 9 & 18 & 27\end{array}\right]
$$

First reduce the matrix to row echelon form, making each pivot equal to $1$.

$$
R_{1}\leftrightarrow R_{2}\qquad M\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -3 & -6 & -9 \\ 4 & -11 & -23 & -33 \\ -3 & 9 & 18 & 27\end{array}\right]
$$



$$
R_{2}:=R_{2}+\left(-4\right)R_{1}\qquad M\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -3 & -6 & -9 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & 3 \\ -3 & 9 & 18 & 27\end{array}\right]
$$



$$
R_{3}:=R_{3}+\left(3\right)R_{1}\qquad M\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -3 & -6 & -9 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{array}\right]
$$

In the row echelon form above, we have only two pivots (in the $1$st and $2$nd columns). To transform the matrix to reduced row echelon form, we need to create zeros above the pivots only.

$$
R_{1}:=R_{1}+\left(3\right)R_{2}\qquad M\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 0 & -3 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{array}\right]

$$
R_{2}:=R_{2}+\left(-1\right)R_{1}\qquad M\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 2 & 4 & 1 \\ 0 & -1 & -3 & 0 \\ -4 & -8 & -16 & -4\end{array}\right]

$$



$$
R_{2}:=\left(-1\right)R_{2}\qquad M\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 2 & 4 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{array}\right]
$$

In the row echelon form above, we have only two pivots (in the $1$st and $2$nd columns). To transform the matrix to reduced row echelon form, we need to create zeros above the pivots only.

$$
R_{1}:=R_{1}+\left(-2\right)R_{2}\qquad M\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 0 & -2 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{array}\right]

question.:question/problem:
Consider the following system of linear equations:

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}- 3 x - 3 y + 6 z &=6 \\ - x + 3 z &=0 \\ x + y - 2 z &=-2\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Use the standard Gauss-Jordan method to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to reduced row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.
question.:question/worked-solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}-3 & -3 & 6 & 6 \\ -1 & 0 & 3 & 0 \\ 1 & 1 & -2 & -2\end{array}\right]
$$

First reduce the matrix to row echelon form, making each pivot equal to $1$.

$$
R_{1}\leftrightarrow R_{3}\qquad M\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 1 & -2 & -2 \\ -1 & 0 & 3 & 0 \\ -3 & -3 & 6 & 6\end{array}\right]
$$



$$
R_{2}:=R_{2}+\left(1\right)R_{1}\qquad M\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 1 & -2 & -2 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & -2 \\ -3 & -3 & 6 & 6\end{array}\right]
$$



$$
R_{3}:=R_{3}+\left(3\right)R_{1}\qquad M\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 1 & -2 & -2 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{array}\right]
$$

In the row echelon form above, we have only two pivots (in the $1$st and $2$nd columns). To transform the matrix to reduced row echelon form, we need to create zeros above the pivots only.

$$
R_{1}:=R_{1}+\left(-1\right)R_{2}\qquad M\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 0 & -3 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{array}\right]
$$

The corresponding system is now

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x - 3 z &=0 \\ y + z &=-2 \\ 0 &=0\end{aligned}\right.
$$

The final equation is $0=0$, so it imposes no restriction. The basic variables are $x$ and $y$, and the free variable is $z$. Find $x$ and $y$ in terms of $z$. Therefore, the general solution is

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x &=3 z \\ y &=- z - 2 \\ z &=z\end{aligned}\right.
$$

where $z$ is an arbitrary real number. In vector form, the solution can be written as

$$
\begin{bmatrix}x \\ y \\ z\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}3 z \\ - z - 2 \\ z\end{bmatrix},\,z\in (-\infty ,\infty )
$$
